[RFCS.19.6] A writer **must not** frame an atom at a field number the registry does not
allocate, and **must** fail rather than emit one. [RFCS.16.3] and [RFCS.18.8] govern a
**reader** meeting such a number; this clause governs the writer, so that an atom nobody
can name cannot be created for the band rules to adjudicate as though a future version had
meant it.

A test needing bytes a later runtime would write therefore frames them by hand from
[RFCS.19.1]'s grammar, naming the field number it claims — so an allocation reaching that
number fails the test rather than turning it into a test of a known atom.
